Subject: Competitive packaging question — CloudThread comparison

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Orchid is running a short bake-off between you and CloudThread; procurement has asked us to get a direct comparison of final economics for their bundled offer (CloudThread Pro + managed connectors) vs Redwood.

Quick context / asks:
- Current CloudThread offer: $0.015 / 1k tokens + $2k / seat for the connectors bundle (annual).
- They included a one-time integration credit and a 10% onboarding discount.

Can Redwood match the headline per-token and provide a clear roll-forward showing: list price, conditional discount path (commit length, usage tiers), and any bundling credit (onboarding / connectors)? We need a figure we can show procurement by EOD Monday.

I've attached the CloudThread SOW we received. Happy to jump on a 30 min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee

Subject: Re: Competitive packaging question — CloudThread comparison

Hi Jordan — great meeting yesterday. Appreciate the SOW.

High-level / quick numbers (prelim, subject to usage profile and model mix):
- List token price (hosted): $0.020 / 1k tokens.
- Conditional discount options we can offer:
  - 18% off list with a 12-month committed spend floor (min $120k ARR),
  - 25% off list for a 24-month commit plus a one-time $15k onboarding credit (applied at first invoice),
  - Alternatively, a blended token + seat bundle: reduce token price to $0.016/1k with a seat fee of $1,250/seat if you take Dedicated connectors.

We can match the CloudThread per-token headline only if Orchid: (a) accepts a 12-month minimum and (b) takes the onboarding credit in lieu of a bigger up-front discount. If you want a straight price match (no commit), we'd need to trade on term length or take a narrower support SLA.

Next steps I need from you to finalize a formal proposal:
- Expected monthly token volume by model type (small / medium / long-context).
- Approx number of seats that need connectors and whether Dedicated capacity is required.
- Target contract length (12 vs 24 months).

I've attached a quick worksheet with scenarios — Connor, Grace: I included a tab with the runtime constraints and the onboarding credit math; please review and flag anything that looks off.

If that looks OK, I can draft a formal offer + DocuSign by tomorrow afternoon. Can we do 11am PT tomorrow to align?

Best,
Tessa Morgan

From: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-04-22T13:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive packaging question — CloudThread comparison

Tessa / Jordan — quick technical note that impacts the bundle economics:

- CloudThread is pricing assuming their connectors run on our smaller GPU profile (A10s equivalent) with heavy token-level caching. Orchid's actual workload (long-context summarization + retrieval-augmented generation) will spend ~60% of tokens in KV cache misses for the first 30 days of indexing. That increases per-token cost on smaller hardware.

- Proposal to preserve the headline token price without exposing Redwood to cost volatility:
  - Offer the 18% 12-month commit, but include a monthly usage true-up if average token CPU/GPU utilization exceeds the forecast by >20% for two consecutive months. The true-up is capped at 5% of the monthly invoice.
  - Alternatively, move connectors to a Dedicated pool (fixed seat fee) — that converts the variable costs to a predictable monthly line item and lets us offer the 24-month 25% discount safely.

I've attached runtime_notes.txt with the assumptions used to model GPU hours vs token counts. If Orchid shares the monthly token mix, I can run a final cost projection and point to the recommended packaging.

Connor O'Brien
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
Attachment: connor_runtime_notes.txt (text)
